suggestions: use window function to compute aggregate in join
reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
compute aggregate in window function to avoid subquery
join customer_address early to filter by state
optimized_sql:
WITH customer_total_return AS (
    SELECT
        agg.ctr_customer_sk,
        agg.ctr_state,
        agg.ctr_total_return,
        AVG(agg.ctr_total_return) OVER (PARTITION BY agg.ctr_state) AS ctr_avg_return
    FROM (
        SELECT
            wr_returning_customer_sk AS ctr_customer_sk,
            ca_state AS ctr_state,
            SUM(wr_return_amt) AS ctr_total_return
        FROM date_dim
        JOIN web_returns ON d_date_sk = wr_returned_date_sk
        JOIN customer_address ON wr_returning_addr_sk = ca_address_sk
        WHERE d_year = 2000
        GROUP BY wr_returning_customer_sk, ca_state
    ) AS agg
)
SELECT
    c_customer_id,
    c_salutation,
    c_first_name,
    c_last_name,
    c_preferred_cust_flag,
    c_birth_day,
    c_birth_month,
    c_birth_year,
    c_birth_country,
    c_login,
    c_email_address,
    c_last_review_date_sk,
    ctr1.ctr_total_return
FROM customer_address
JOIN customer ON ca_address_sk = c_current_addr_sk AND ca_state = 'AR'
JOIN customer_total_return ctr1 ON ctr1.ctr_customer_sk = c_customer_sk
WHERE ctr1.ctr_state IS NOT NULL
  AND ctr1.ctr_total_return > ctr1.ctr_avg_return * 1.2
ORDER BY
    c_customer_id,
    c_salutation,
    c_first_name,
    c_last_name,
    c_preferred_cust_flag,
    c_birth_day,
    c_birth_month,
    c_birth_year,
    c_birth_country,
    c_login,
    c_email_address,
    c_last_review_date_sk,
    ctr1.ctr_total_return
LIMIT 100
